column1: # CONTROLS FOR THE SPLIT GATE ONLY (cert_gate_split.sh).
# Separated from cert-controls.tsv on 2026-08-01: cert_gate_fork.sh reads that
# file WHOLESALE with FORK includes, so split-only controls failed there with
# "cannot locate theory C10DeployedInstance" -- a reason mismatch that turned
# the sibling gate RED.  My run-2 remediation broke the fork gate; found by
# MUST-FAIL checks the declared proof-driver rejection, not logical falsity of
# the attempted statement. Exact-term mismatch can also reject a true weaker
# statement. Evidence classes and limitations: CONTROL-EVIDENCE.md.
# A/B/C each delete exactly ONE hypothesis of badenc_game_hoare + badenc_is_one;
# D mutates the CONCLUSION 1%r -> 0%r.  Reasons observed, not assumed.
# NOTE ON C: `nothing to rewrite` is shape-adjacent, and the gate's own PHASE 3
# comment warns about exactly that.  It is nonetheless a genuine deletion failure:
# the site it breaks is `by rewrite /P -hcol; move: hP; rewrite /P`, i.e. the ONLY
# place `P cm` is consumed to produce the game's `P m /\ P m'` conjunct.  Verified
# by reading the failing line, not inferred from the message.
# A drops the GRIND-REACHABILITY premise, B drops forger losslessness, C drops ONE
# of the six WOTS-TW separations from F.  Reasons observed, not assumed.
# HONEST LIMITATION: A and B fail with the SAME message ("this proof-term proves:"),
# so the gate's reason check cannot tell them apart -- it only confirms each failed
# at a PROOF-TERM mismatch rather than a parse error or a missing require.  What
# distinguishes them is WHICH premise was deleted, which is fixed by the generator,
# not by the message.  Recorded rather than papered over.
# TRAP, paid for on the first run (RED, 1 failure): the gate matches the reason against
# the FIRST `[critical]` line only (`grep -a '^\[critical\]' | head -1`), and EasyCrypt
# WRAPS long module lists across lines.  C's declared reason was originally
# "is not allowed to use the modules(s)" -- true of the diagnostic, but on its SECOND
# line, so the gate scored it as failing for the wrong reason.  Declare a substring of
# the FIRST line, and avoid line numbers in it (they drift when the file is edited).
# A drops the CHARGED WOTS LEG from the composition; B drops the deployed statement.
# A IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: a green compile there would mean the substitution of four
# named terms for the opaque game does nothing, i.e. the theorem is vacuous.
# --- T_COLL_RES_ENUM chain controls, promoted 2026-09-14 with cdrafts-split/{TCollResEnum,
# The mutation specs are copied BY SCRIPT from the experiment generators, and
# scratch/check_tcoll_ctls_match.py asserts each control equals the experiment control
# with comments stripped (21/21).  All 21 were RE-RUN against the LIVE trees before
# promotion (WOTS_C_Real.ec and WOTS_TW_ES.ec had changed since 2026-08-14): every
# first [critical] line matched the experiment receipt exactly.  Reasons observed.
# HONEST LIMITATION, same as the wlc controls: many share "this proof-term proves:" or
# "cannot prove goal (strict)", so the reason check confirms the KIND of failure
# (a proof-term mismatch / an unprovable goal, not a parse error or a missing require);
# WHICH fact was deleted is fixed by the generator, not by the message.
# tcoll_ctlF "not an equation to rewrite" is shape-adjacent, like badenc_ctlC: it breaks
# `rewrite -h5` in tcoll_win_needs_coll, the only consumer of tcoll_wf's second conjunct.
# bered_ctlZ is the anti-fail-open canary (`lemma NEGCTL : false` by `trivial`).
# bes4_ctlG is a NECESSITY control on a proof step (s4_transfer removed from
# badenc_le_tcoll's closing smt), not an information deletion -- see BadEncStep4.ec.
# A drops `badenc_le_tcoll` from the composition -- THE ONE THAT MATTERS: a green compile
# would mean the T_COLL term replaces the BadEnc term without doing anything.  B drops the
# WOTSNAMED statement.  C drops the ONE new separation, -O_TCollEnum_Default, from F.
# C's first generator left a dangling comma and failed with `parse error` -- a SYNTAX failure
# that proves nothing about the restriction.  Caught by reading the reason before
# registering; regenerated, it fails at the restriction check.  Reasons observed; C's
# declared substring is from the FIRST [critical] line, which EasyCrypt wraps.
# --- SCOPE-ISOLATION controls for the last admit, added 2026-09-15.
# FORS_C_TreePort.ec holds extract_op, the only admit.  Each NEGATIVE requires a headline theory
# and names a TreePort symbol; EasyCrypt must report it UNKNOWN -- the theory is not loaded in the
# headline environment, so no tactic (bare smt() included) can use the admit.  Each has a MUST-PASS
# twin differing by ONE require (FORS_C_TreePort added), so the negative fails for SCOPE and not
# for syntax.  _scope_env_n_m shows `require GprocTCollNamed.` makes a dependency 3 require-hops
# deep resolvable, so the negatives test the FULL environment, not a smaller one.  GprocTCollNamed
# alone: the other five headline files are in its require-cone -- stops being true if the family
# stops being a chain.  TRIPWIRE: if any file in that cone ever requires FORS_C_TreePort, the
# negatives COMPILE and this phase goes RED.  The census would not notice that edit (TreePort is
# already a closure root).  Reasons observed 2026-09-15 in ec-grind (r2026.02), not assumed.
# --- PER-FILE scope negatives, added 2026-09-15 (later).  The block above relied on the other five
# headline files sitting in GprocTCollNamed's require-cone.  Kimi K3 (adversarial review) found that
# chain UNGUARDED: all six headline files are closure roots, so one could leave the cone with nothing
# going RED and then require FORS_C_TreePort.  Each headline file now has its OWN negative.  They
# share the op-form twin _scope_pos_op.ec: the body is byte-identical, and any failure OTHER than the
# declared unknown-symbol one (a name clash, a syntax error, the headline theory failing to load) is
# graded WRONG REASON, i.e. RED -- so per-file twins would add rows, not information.  Reasons
# observed in ec-grind for all six theories in the 2026-09-15 feasibility run.
# NOT COVERED: a SEVENTH headline file -- nothing yet links tools/taint_closure.py's HEADLINE list to
# [UPDATE 2026-09-15 (third): COVERED.  tools/taint_closure.py --check now requires an EXACT bijection
# between the files declaring HEADLINE results and the scratch/_scope_neg_op_<H>.ec rows here: each
# row MUST-FAIL, its reason naming every admit theory, its probe requiring its own headline theory.
# A new headline file with no row, or a row for a file that declares none, is RED in PHASE 5.
# Controls T11..T14 in scratch/taint_controls.sh.  Rows in this file are read by that check: keep the
# --- C10SurfaceKernel,C10Surface}.ec.  Reasons OBSERVED under the pinned image, not assumed.
# KctlC: complement symmetry d |-> 7-d maps sum 205 to itself.  KctlE: small-scale true value 0.
# KctlD/CtlSum204/CtlLen42/CtlVal each perturb one input (steps, target sum, word length, value).
# KctlA and KctlB are DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED.  Both fail -- but with
# `anomaly: Stack overflow`, not a proof failure, at full 43/205 scale (observed today AND in
# the original 2026-08-14 receipt: WALL_MS 42763/41990).  A stack overflow does not
# DISCRIMINATE: it would occur just the same if count_ds were broken into computing garbage,
# so registering it would buy a control that fails for a reason unrelated to the property.
# CtlVal perturbs the same value and fails cleanly, so the property is covered.
# Concrete digit consumer and explicit IID failure mass (observed proof failures).
